bench-and-bill.title: Judge rules Ferngrove's app store rules broke antitrust law
bench-and-bill.author: Celia Marchetti
body: [f01: A federal judge ruled on Friday that Ferngrove's rules for its Canopy app store broke antitrust law.] [f02: The case was brought by Kettlebrook Games, a mobile game publisher.]
[f03: The judge ordered Ferngrove to let apps offer payment options other than its own.] [f04: Ferngrove has 90 days to comply.]

[f05: “We strongly disagree with this decision, which puts the people who use our phones at risk, and we will appeal,” a Ferngrove spokesperson said.] Either way, this fight is far from over, and the order itself is the part app developers will read most closely.

byteward.title: Ferngrove's app store rules broke antitrust law, judge rules
byteward.author: Simone Achterberg
body: [f01: A federal judge has ruled that the rules for Ferngrove's Canopy app store violate antitrust law.] [f05: Ferngrove says it will appeal.]

[f06: Canopy is currently the only way to install apps on Ferngrove phones.] [f07: The ruling doesn't require Ferngrove to allow apps from other sources.] That leaves the biggest question for another day, and probably another case.

launch-desk.title: Judge rules against Ferngrove's app store rules
launch-desk.author: Inez Calder
body: [f01: A judge has found that Ferngrove's Canopy app store rules broke antitrust law.] The money at stake is large.
[f08: Ferngrove's standard cut of in-app purchases is 30%.] [f09: Canopy brought in $11.4 billion in commissions last year.]
[f10: Ferngrove shares fell 5% in afternoon trading after the ruling.] Investors can do the math.

frametime.title: Judge says Ferngrove's app store rules broke antitrust law
frametime.author: Kofi Mensah-Lind
body: [f01: A federal judge says Ferngrove's Canopy app store rules broke antitrust law.] For game studios, this one is about money.

[f08: Today, Ferngrove's standard cut is 30% of each in-app purchase.] [f13: Developers earning under $1 million a year pay a reduced 15% rate.] [f14: Kettlebrook, which brought the case, paid Ferngrove $214 million in commissions last year, according to trial testimony.]

[f03: Under the order, games can offer players their own checkout instead of Ferngrove's.] That sounds like a windfall. [f15: But the ruling doesn't say whether Ferngrove can still take a fee on those outside purchases.] Studios shouldn't redo their budgets just yet.

ohm-and-bit.title: Judge rules Ferngrove's Canopy store broke antitrust law
ohm-and-bit.author: Imogen Vale
body: [f01: A federal judge ruled on Friday that Ferngrove's Canopy app store rules broke antitrust law.] What does that change on the phone itself?
[f03: The order lets apps offer payment options besides Ferngrove's own.] [f11: Ferngrove's software already lets apps open web pages, so outside checkouts need only a rule change, not new code.]

Installing apps from elsewhere is a different story. [f06: Ferngrove phones refuse to install any app that didn't come from Canopy.] [f07: Nothing in the ruling forces Ferngrove to accept apps from outside Canopy.]
[f12: Ferngrove's own developer tools can already load apps from outside Canopy onto test phones.] The capability is there. What's missing is permission.

wirefold.title: Judge rules Ferngrove app store rules broke antitrust law
body: A federal judge ruled on Friday that Ferngrove's rules for its Canopy app store broke antitrust law, handing a win to the game publisher that sued the company.
